newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-HALL COMEBACK WIN FAILS TO UPSET SOUTH KOREA.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-HALL COMEBACK WIN FAILS TO UPSET SOUTH KOREA.

text.p: England's Darren Hall marked his comeback from injury by defeating world silver medallist Park Sung-woo but could not prevent South Korea from opening their Sudirman Cup world team championship campaign with a 4-1 victory on Wednesday.

The South Koreans, twice former winners, clinched the win in the fourth match when All-England champions Kang Kyung-jin and Ha Tae-kwon defeated Simon Archer and Chris Hunt 15-8 15-8 in the men's doubles.

England, who had already lost to defending champions China, now face a group one relegation play-off against Sweden, themselves suffering their second defeat of the tournament at the hands of Denmark.

South Korea, who meet China on Thursday for a place in the semifinals, won the opening mixed doubles but Hall raised hopes of an upset win for England with a stunning 15-10 17-15 victory over Park, the world number eight.

It was an extraordinary result for Hall, the 1990 European champion, who has dropped to number 57 in the world and was playing his first major event after three months sidelined by an Achilles injury.

In the opening game he surged into a 5-0 lead and stayed ahead throughout. The second game was more of a roller-coaster. Park took the first five points without reply but Hall hit back to lead 7-5 and 9-8.

The game then turned in Park's favour and the Korean held five game points at 14-9 before Hall staged another remarkable recovery to win. In the women's singles, Kim Ji-hyun put South Korea back in front with an 11-5 11-1 win over Julia Mann and that set the stage for the men's doubles pair to secure overall victory.
Denmark, bronze medallists two years ago, opened their bid for a first triumph in the Sudirman Cup by defeating Sweden in double-quick time.

The Danes, despite resting Olympic champion Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen ahead of Thursday's match against Indonesia, won the opening three rubbers in straight games to ensure sweet revenge over their Scandinavian rivals. They went on to win the tie 4-1.
The last time the two countries met in Glasgow, Sweden scored a shock win in the final of the 1992 European championship.

But there was never any hint of a repeat. Camilla Martin set the reigning European champions on the road to victory with an 11-3 11-3 win in just 13 minutes over Marina Andrievskaya, a former Russian who now lives in Sweden.

Michael Sogaard and Rikke Olsen then beat Jens Olsson and Astrid Crabo 15-6 15-3 in the mixed doubles. In the absence of Hoyer-Larsen, world number 10 Thomas Stuer-Lauridsen clinched Denmark's win in the men's singles against Rikard Magnusson.

Magnusson, ranked 24 places lower than the Dane, seized a 5-0 lead in the opening game but Stuer-Lauridsen hit back, drawing level at 9-9 before going on to take the game 18-14. The second game was no contest, with the tall Dane taking it 15-1 in just six minutes.
Sweden had already lost to Indonesia.
